Fashion Professor Mallory Made Her Own Wedding Dress

DIY & Handmade
Mansion
USAVirginia
Summer
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:55
Instaread

Mallory and Jon were married on 26th July 2025 at Mankin Mansion in Richmond, Virginia, a historic house that was just the right size for their guests and so full of character it barely needed dressing at all. Their day was photographed by Kaitlyn Burdette Photography, whose work Mallory had followed for a while before booking her, and whose film photography is absolutely beautiful.

Mallory is a fashion professor, and when it came to her own wedding dress there was only ever one person who could make it. She designed and made the gown herself and wore it with a cathedral-length veil, while her favourite blue found its way into just about everything else.

The couple first met on Hinge, bonding over the arts and a shared sense of humour, and Jon proposed at a picnic in Byrd Park in May 2023 with a little help from their friends. Here, Mallory tells the rest of their story.

The Dress

Made by the bride

I designed and made my own dress entirely from scratch. I was a fashion design student at university and am now a fashion professor.

People kept asking me if I was going to make my dress, and I eventually decided I had to because no one else would be able to execute my vision exactly as I imagined. I hand-beaded everything and constructed the whole dress in about six months.

Designing and making my own wedding dress was a challenge I wanted to pursue ever since I was a design student at Virginia Commonwealth University.

I have always loved bridal design and have taken on several other clients since making my gown. The process was long… a very intense amount of hours went into the beading process in particular. I wore a cathedral length veil from an Etsy shop.

Jon’s outfit came from Jos. A. Bank, and my hair and make-up were done by Avenue 42

My father walked me down the aisle to Stand By Me (the Florence & The Machine cover). Our ceremony was officiated by Daniel Timms. We wrote our own vows and got Jon’s uncle to officiate and read a story/poem.

The Photography

Kaitlyn Burdette Photography

Our wedding was photographed by Kaitlyn Burdette Photography. Kaitlyn is very professional and extremely talented. I had been following her work for a while, so it was a no brainer when we chose her. Her film photography is amazing!

Kaitlyn Burdette Photography

How They Met

Jon and I met on Hinge when I was 21, and he was 22. We bonded over the arts, as well as our shared sense of humour. We got engaged in May 2023. He planned a picnic for us in Byrd Park, and had my housemate take photos, and his housemate record the whole proposal.

I suspected something was going to happen the whole day, but I was still completely surprised when our friends jumped out of the bushes with cameras, and he pulled out the ring.

The Reception

Mankin Mansion was the perfect size for our guest count. We love all the adornments and the fact that we did not have to do much to dress it up.

Our flowers were by Vogue Flowers, and Deep Run Roadhouse took care of the catering, with our cake from Publix. Our stationery was designed by Alexis O’Neill, and our entertainment came from The Masters of the Ceremony

My favourite parts were dancing until my knees gave out, and the initial moments after the ceremony, when Jon and I got to let it all sink in.

If I could do anything differently, I would have ditched my veil haha. It just got in the way and I took it off right after the ceremony.

Words of Wedded Wisdom

Don’t let others convince you to add add add when it comes to decor, services etc. If you have good food, good music, good drinks, and good people, it will be a good time.

Meet The Author

Annabel
Founder of Love My Dress, podcaster and editor, Annabel lives in rural North Yorkshire with her husband and business partner Philip, their two daughters, one at university and one aged 15, and a lively menagerie of furry hounds. She loves photography, meditation, long walks, being outdoors and star gazing. She also has a slightly unexpected obsession with blockchain and market analysis, studying price charts and patterns and has a deep fascination with market psychology. Annabel is known for her integrity, trust and advocacy within the wedding industry, values that underpin both her editorial voice and professional relationships. Alongside her work on Love My Dress, she also supports Philip in running the family’s sustainable flower farm and floral design business, Moonwind Flowers.
